title: LServe: Efficient Long-sequence LLM Serving with Unified Sparse Attention
quote: we find that only a constant number of KV pages is required to preserve long-context and reasoning capabilities, irrespective of context length
proves: Serving-integrated hybrid sparse attention (half the heads become streaming heads, plus hierarchical query-centric KV page selection); 2.9x prefill and 1.3-2.1x decode speedup over vLLM with accuracy maintained.
does_not_prove: Gains reported against vLLM on long-context benchmarks; abstract gives no mixed-workload, short-request, or high-concurrency preemption study. The constant-page claim is a workload assumption that adversarial or aggregation-heavy inputs could break; untested here.
bearing: serving-integrated sparse attention; fixed page budget assumption

title: MagicPIG: LSH Sampling for Efficient LLM Generation
quote: TopK attention itself suffers from quality degradation in certain downstream tasks because attention is not always as sparse as expected
proves: Shows TopK sparse attention (the basis of Quest-style serving) degrades on some tasks because attention is not always sparse; LSH sampling on CPU gives up to 5x decode throughput.
does_not_prove: Does not characterize which workloads are dense in the wild; no multi-tenant serving or preemption study.
bearing: workload dependence of sparsity; TopK failure mode; CPU-GPU heterogeneous serving

title: ShadowKV: KV Cache in Shadows for High-Throughput Long-Context LLM Inference
venue: arXiv 2410.21465 (ICML 2025 per secondary sources; not confirmed on abstract page)
quote: support up to 6$\times$ larger batch sizes and boost throughput by up to 3.04$\times$ on an A100 GPU without sacrificing accuracy
proves: Low-rank key cache plus CPU-offloaded values with sparse reconstruction; claims 6x batch size and 3.04x throughput on RULER, LongBench, NIAH.
does_not_prove: Benchmarks are long-context retrieval/QA; no long-output, reasoning, or mixed-length serving traces; not integrated into vLLM/SGLang.
bearing: throughput claim; batch-size gains; benchmark-limited evidence

title: Quest: Query-Aware Sparsity for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference
quote: we observe the criticality of a token highly depends on the query
proves: Token criticality depends on the query; page-level min/max key bounds select Top-K pages; 7.03x latency reduction. Quest is one of the sparse families HiSparse later integrates into SGLang.
does_not_prove: Keeps full KV in GPU memory (reduces bandwidth, not capacity); single-request latency, no batched serving or workload-mix study.
bearing: query-dependent sparsity; compute-vs-capacity distinction

title: InfiniGen: Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models with Dynamic KV Cache Management
quote: improves the overall performance of a modern offloading-based system by up to 3.00x compared to prior KV cache management methods
proves: Speculative prefetch of important KV entries in offloading-based serving; up to 3x over prior KV management with better accuracy.
does_not_prove: Offloading setting (FlexGen-style), not continuous-batching GPU serving; no workload-shift or adversarial-input evaluation.
bearing: offload plus selective fetch; systems venue evidence

title: DuoAttention: Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference with Retrieval and Streaming Heads
quote: DuoAttention uses a lightweight, optimization-based algorithm with synthetic data to identify retrieval heads accurately
proves: Static head split (retrieval vs streaming) identified offline on synthetic data; up to 2.55x (MHA) / 1.67x (GQA) memory reduction.
does_not_prove: Head identification is calibrated offline on synthetic data; the abstract does not test whether the head split holds on out-of-distribution inputs (code, multilingual, multi-turn). That transfer question is open.
bearing: offline calibration; static head budget; OOD transfer untested

title: RazorAttention: Efficient KV Cache Compression Through Retrieval Heads
quote: reduction in KV cache size by over 70% without noticeable impacts on performance
proves: Training-free retrieval-head split with compensation token; over 70% KV reduction, FlashAttention compatible.
does_not_prove: No serving-level throughput or workload-variance evaluation in abstract; head set fixed per model, not per input.
bearing: static head split; plug-and-play claim

title: R-KV: Redundancy-aware KV Cache Compression for Reasoning Models
quote: it can also lead to reasoning failures when deployed with existing KV cache compression approaches
proves: Existing compression baselines reach only ~60% of full-cache performance on reasoning traces at 10% budget; R-KV keeps ~100% and claims 6.6x throughput.
does_not_prove: Only two math datasets; not integrated into a serving engine (Zipage notes R-KV is not engine-integrated).
bearing: workload shift: long decode/reasoning breaks prefill-era compression

title: KV-Compress: Paged KV-Cache Compression with Variable Compression Rates per Attention Head
quote: application of such a strategy within existing inference frameworks adds fragmentation and cannot realize the theoretical compression rates in physical memory
proves: Head-variable eviction in PagedAttention; vLLM integration raises total throughput up to 5.18x by enabling larger decode batches; 64x keeps >90% performance on all but three LongBench subsets.
does_not_prove: The gain is conditional on memory-bound batching; the abstract does not say how it behaves under preemption, prefix caching, or short-prompt workloads.
bearing: serving integration; fragmentation; per-subset variance

title: PagedEviction: Structured Block-wise KV Cache Pruning for Efficient Large Language Model Inference
venue: arXiv 2509.04377 (preprint; EACL 2026 Findings per secondary source, not confirmed)
quote: integrates seamlessly with PagedAttention without requiring any modifications to its CUDA attention kernels
proves: Block-wise eviction aligned with vLLM pages, no kernel changes; better memory/accuracy than baselines on LongBench with 1B-8B Llama models.
does_not_prove: LongBench only; no throughput-under-load, multi-turn, or prefix-sharing interaction study.
bearing: vLLM-native eviction

title: Zipage: Maintain High Request Concurrency for LLM Reasoning through Compressed PagedAttention
quote: most of them are impractical for industrial-grade applications
proves: Engine with token-wise eviction inside PagedAttention plus scheduling, prefix caching and async compression; ~95% of full-KV accuracy, >2.1x speedup on large-scale math reasoning.
does_not_prove: Evaluated on math reasoning only; abstract gives no mixed workload or tail-latency results.
bearing: serving-integrated decode-time eviction; workload-specific evaluation

title: Tangram: Unlocking Non-Uniform KV Cache Compression for Efficient Multi-turn LLM Serving
quote: spends up to 25% of prefill time reclaiming scattered pages, and skews GPU workloads that inflate decode latency by up to $1.7\times$
proves: Quantifies serving costs of non-uniform (per-head) compression in vLLM: fragmentation, 25% prefill time on page reclamation, up to 1.7x decode latency inflation. Claims head ranking is input-invariant and calibratable from 50 samples; 2.6x throughput over full KV.
does_not_prove: The input-invariance claim is tested on its calibration and eval sets, not under deliberate distribution shift; robustness of the static budget to OOD inputs is an assumption a gap study could attack.
bearing: serving overhead of adaptive budgets; input-invariance claim (testable)

title: GrowPage: On-Demand KV Budgeting for Efficient LLM Reasoning Serving
quote: reasoning workloads exhibit substantial demand variation: different requests require different KV capacities
proves: Per-request KV capacity grows on demand during decode, integrated with PagedAttention, keeping continuous batching and prefix caching.
does_not_prove: Reasoning benchmarks only; abstract does not show behavior when many requests grow simultaneously (capacity contention), or adversarial demand growth.
bearing: input-dependent budget in serving; demand variance evidence; contention risk

title: Benchmarking KV-Cache Optimizations across Task Quality and System Performance for Long-Context Serving
quote: CaM yields large gains on selected QA workloads but exhibits substantial workload sensitivity in both quality and realized compression ratio
proves: Serving benchmark of KIVI, TurboQuant, SnapKV, CaM across LongBench workload types and context buckets: compression ratio alone poorly predicts end-to-end performance; realized compression ratio itself varies by workload.
does_not_prove: Two 7-8B models and LongBench-style tasks; no reasoning, multi-turn, or adversarial workload; no preemption analysis in abstract.
bearing: direct evidence: gains vary by workload; realized ratio is workload-dependent

title: KVServe: Service-Aware KV Cache Compression for Communication-Efficient Disaggregated LLM Serving
quote: Existing KV compression are typically static runtime configurations, despite production service context varies over time in workload mix, bandwidth, and SLO/quality budgets
proves: Adaptive online selection of KV communication compression in vLLM PD-disaggregated serving using a bandit controller; states that a fixed compression choice can increase latency as workload mix shifts.
does_not_prove: Compression of KV in transit (network/storage), not on-GPU attention-state eviction; quality-budget robustness under OOD prompts not addressed in abstract.
bearing: adaptive compression under workload-mix shift; production-context argument

title: Joint Encoding of KV-Cache Blocks for Scalable LLM Serving
quote: fuses similar blocks across requests and input chunks into shared representations
proves: Cross-request block fusion; up to 4.38x compression and ~40% token throughput gain on single-machine vLLM.
does_not_prove: Gain depends on similarity across concurrent requests, so it should vary with workload diversity; abstract does not test low-similarity or adversarial mixes. Cross-request fusion also couples tenants (isolation question).
bearing: workload-dependent gain (cross-request similarity); multi-tenant coupling

title: EVICPRESS: Joint KV-Cache Compression and Eviction for Efficient LLM Serving
quote: applying conservative compression to contexts that are sensitive to compression errors
proves: Per-context utility profiling decides compression level and tier placement; up to 2.19x faster TTFT at equal quality on 12 datasets, 5 models. Explicitly treats compression sensitivity as context-dependent.
does_not_prove: Profiling is periodic; abstract does not test how quickly profiles go stale under workload shift or adversarial contexts.
bearing: context-dependent sensitivity; adaptive compression plus eviction; profile staleness

title: HiSparse: Scaling Sparse-Attention Decoding with Hierarchical KV Cache Management
quote: decoding hits a capacity wall long before it runs out of compute
proves: Top-k sparse attention (DSA, NSA, Quest) reduces compute but not HBM capacity; HiSparse keeps full KV on host with a fixed GPU cache and LRU, merged into upstream SGLang, up to 4.7x peak throughput.
does_not_prove: Exact (lossless) placement, so no accuracy risk; performance depends on top-k hit rate, which is workload-dependent and not characterized across access patterns.
bearing: production integration (SGLang); miss-rate workload dependence

title: HiSparse: Turbocharging Sparse Attention with Hierarchical Memory (LMSYS blog)
quote: As a result, sparse attention is often capacity-bound rather than compute-bound, limiting the achievable batch size and overall throughput.
proves: Production adoption: experimental SGLang feature for DSA models (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.1); >3x baseline at 256 concurrency; modest overhead at low concurrency from top-k misses; miss counts reported only on LongBenchV2.
does_not_prove: Miss behavior shown on one benchmark only; no shifted or adversarial access patterns.
bearing: production adoption; load-dependent gain; LRU miss sensitivity

title: Sparse Attention in TensorRT LLM (tech blog 17)
quote: n/a (WebFetch summary; no verbatim sentence captured)
proves: Production integration of RocketKV, DSA and Skip Softmax in TensorRT-LLM. RocketKV on B200: ~1.5% LongBench drop; throughput gain grows with length (Llama3.1-8B 1.40x at 8k/1k, 2.26x at 32k/4k; 70B TP4 only 1.05x at 8k/1k). Smaller speedup at low batch; RocketKV cache manager lacks KV reuse and disaggregated serving support.
does_not_prove: Vendor benchmark; no workload-shift or tail-latency study; quote not captured verbatim (re-fetch before citing).
bearing: production adoption; gain depends on length, batch, model size; feature interactions

title: DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp in vLLM: Fine-Grained Sparse Attention in Action
quote: We are still in the process of verifying vLLM's implementation against the official accuracy results.
proves: Production adoption of model-native sparse attention (top-2048 tokens via lightning indexer); indexer adds its own K cache per token; block size fixed at 64; high batch plus long context materializes a logits tensor before top-k (performance concern).
does_not_prove: Does not quantify memory effect or accuracy across workloads.
bearing: production adoption; extra indexer cache; batch x length cost

title: Optimizing Inference for Long Context and Large Batch Sizes with NVFP4 KV Cache
quote: NVFP4 cuts KV cache memory footprint by up to 50% and can effectively double context budgets
proves: Production KV quantization (4-bit) on Blackwell; <1% loss on code, knowledge and long-context benchmarks; largest drop on Ruler 64K (~1 pt, read from figure); up to 3x lower TTFT via higher cache hit rate; MXFP4 ~5 pts worse on MMLU.
does_not_prove: Vendor evidence on few benchmarks; per-task numbers read from a chart; no reasoning-length or multilingual tests.
bearing: production adoption; per-task variance small but largest on long context

title: NVFP4 KV cache in SGLang (LMSYS blog)
quote: The current NVFP4 KV support in SGLang is experimental.
proves: SGLang NVFP4 KV dtype: decode throughput +26-30% at fixed concurrency, +37-78% at iso-capacity (32K-1M); largest accuracy drop on SWE-bench Verified (~1.6 pts vs FP8); agentic gains appear only above ~12 concurrency and depend on prefix reuse pattern.
does_not_prove: Two models, small task set; no needle/long-context accuracy test; figures from WebFetch summary (verify model names before citing).
bearing: production adoption; gain depends on concurrency and reuse pattern; coding task most sensitive

title: Quantized KV Cache (vLLM docs)
quote: Some attention layer types (e.g. sliding-window) are more sensitive to KV-cache quantization.
proves: vLLM ships FP8 KV cache; without calibration all scales default to 1.0; calibration via llm-compressor recommended; per-layer skip flag exists because some layer types are more sensitive.
does_not_prove: No accuracy numbers; calibration-set dependence (scales from one dataset) is not discussed.
bearing: production default; calibration dependence

title: QServe: W4A8KV4 Quantization and System Co-design for Efficient LLM Serving
quote: state-of-the-art INT4 quantization techniques only accelerate low-batch, edge LLM inference, failing to deliver performance gains in large-batch, cloud-based LLM serving
proves: Shows paper-level quantization gains fail to transfer to large-batch serving due to 20-90% dequant overhead; KV4 with SmoothAttention gives 1.2-3.5x max throughput vs TensorRT-LLM.
does_not_prove: Quality evaluated on standard benchmarks; no workload-shift analysis.
bearing: paper claims vs serving reality (quantization)

title: RocketKV: Accelerating Long-Context LLM Inference via Two-Stage KV Cache Compression
quote: We also propose a variant of RocketKV for multi-turn scenarios
proves: Two-stage eviction plus hybrid top-k sparse attention; up to 400x compression, 3.7x speedup; separate multi-turn variant needed. Later integrated into TensorRT-LLM.
does_not_prove: Need for a multi-turn variant implies the base method is workload-specific; serving-level results in TRT-LLM are smaller than paper peak.
bearing: paper vs production gap; multi-turn sensitivity

title: How Query Visibility Changes KV-Cache Compression Rankings: A Matched-Budget Audit
quote: the most widely deployed method, SnapKV, loses to "keep the start and the recent window" on average (-0.066)
proves: Under query-agnostic compression (the reuse deployment case), rankings flip; SnapKV drops +0.198 between protocols and loses to a trivial baseline; only KeyDiff consistently beats trivial baselines. 144k paired evals with bootstrap.
does_not_prove: Accuracy only (RULER-8192, LongBench), 7-9B models; no serving throughput.
bearing: evaluation protocol shift; deployment-relevant degradation; strong methodology precedent

title: EpiCache: Episodic KV Cache Management for Long-Term Conversation on Resource-Constrained Environments
quote: query-dependent eviction narrows the cache semantics to a single query, leading to failure cases in multi-turn conversations
proves: Multi-turn failure of query-dependent eviction; episodic clustering improves accuracy up to 30% on LongMemEval, Realtalk, LoCoMo at 4-6x compression; notes post-prefill eviction has unbounded peak memory.
does_not_prove: Single-user on-device setting; no multi-tenant serving.
bearing: multi-turn degradation; peak-memory caveat of prefill eviction

title: SONIC: Segmented Optimized Nexus for Information Compression in Key-Value Caching
quote: Existing KV cache compression methods often fail to account for the structural properties of multi-turn dialogues
proves: Learned multi-turn compression beats H2O and StreamingLLM by 35.55% on MTBench101 at 50-80% compression.
does_not_prove: Learned method needs training; heuristic-baseline gap is the evidence of interest, not the method.
bearing: multi-turn degradation of heuristic eviction

title: Hold Onto That Thought: Assessing KV Cache Compression On Reasoning
venue: arXiv 2512.12008; NeurIPS 2025 virtual listing (likely workshop, not confirmed)
quote: eviction strategies at low budgets can produce longer reasoning traces, revealing a tradeoff between cache size and inference costs
proves: For non-reasoning Llama-3.1-8B no single strategy wins and results depend heavily on dataset type; for reasoning models H2O and decode-time SnapKV dominate; low budgets lengthen reasoning traces.
does_not_prove: Accuracy and trace length only; no serving throughput measurement of the length-inflation cost.
bearing: per-task variance; output-length inflation under compression (serving cost)

title: ThinKV: Thought-Adaptive KV Cache Compression for Efficient Reasoning Models
quote: attention sparsity reveals distinct thought types with varying importance within the CoT
proves: Hybrid quantization-eviction keyed to thought type, with a PagedAttention-extending kernel reusing evicted slots; <5% KV with near-lossless accuracy and up to 5.8x throughput over baselines on math and code.
does_not_prove: Thought-type classifier tuned on reasoning traces; behavior on non-reasoning or mixed workloads not shown.
bearing: reasoning-aware compression; serving kernel

title: G-KV: Decoding-Time KV Cache Eviction with Global Attention
quote: existing methods often focus on prompt compression or token eviction with local attention score, overlooking the long-term importance of tokens
proves: Decode-time eviction for reasoning combining local and historical attention; adds RL and distillation to adapt models to compressed caches.
does_not_prove: Abstract gives no numbers; model post-training makes it less of a drop-in serving option.
bearing: decode-time eviction for reasoning

title: LazyEviction: Lagged KV Eviction with Attention Pattern Observation for Efficient Long Reasoning
venue: arXiv 2506.15969 (ACL 2026 long per ACL Anthology preview)
quote: a large proportion of tokens regain high attention after multiple decoding steps
proves: Token Importance Recurrence in reasoning traces breaks greedy eviction; lagged eviction keeps 50-70% reduction with comparable accuracy.
does_not_prove: No serving integration; reasoning workloads only.
bearing: workload-specific attention dynamics (reasoning)

title: Which Heads Matter for Reasoning? RL-Guided KV Cache Compression (RLKV)
quote: head-reallocation methods, designed for retrieval tasks, fail to preserve the heads essential for generative reasoning
proves: Retrieval-head selection (DuoAttention/RazorAttention style) does not transfer to reasoning; RL-found reasoning heads allow 20-60% reduction, up to 2.06x end-to-end speedup.
does_not_prove: Head selection is per model; transfer to other workload types not shown.
bearing: head-budget transfer failure across task types

title: Kitty: Accurate and Efficient 2-bit KV Cache Quantization with Dynamic Channel-wise Precision Boost
quote: While 4-bit KV quantization preserves accuracy, 2-bit often degrades it, especially on long-context reasoning
proves: 2-bit KV quantization degrades most on long-context reasoning (secondary summary: KIVI-K2V2 ~13 pts below FP16 on AIME with 32k generations); mixed-precision paged layout gives up to 8x batch and 2.1-4.1x throughput.
does_not_prove: AIME figure from search summary, not verified in PDF.
bearing: quantization fragility on long decode; serving co-design

title: KVarN: Variance-Normalized KV-Cache Quantization Mitigates Error Accumulation in Reasoning Tasks
quote: current methods are evaluated under prefill-like settings and errors behave differently under autoregressive decoding
proves: KV quantization errors accumulate over decode steps (driven by token-scale errors); prefill-style evaluation hides this. vLLM implementation released.
does_not_prove: Math and HumanEval only; no serving throughput in abstract.
bearing: evaluation-regime shift (prefill vs decode); quantization error accumulation

title: MixKVQ: Query-Aware Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization for Long-Context Reasoning
venue: arXiv 2512.19206 (ACL 2026 long per ACL Anthology preview)
quote: existing low-bit quantization methods often exhibit severe performance degradation on complex reasoning tasks
proves: Low-bit KV quantization fails on reasoning due to key outlier channels; query-aware channel precision fixes it.
does_not_prove: No serving evaluation; reasoning datasets only.
bearing: quantization fragility by task type

title: KV-CoRE: Benchmarking Data-Dependent Low-Rank Compressibility of KV-Caches in LLMs
quote: uncovering systematic patterns that link compressibility to model architecture, training data, and language coverage
proves: Only large-scale evidence found on language dependence: KV compressibility measured over 5 English domains and 16 languages; Normalized Effective Rank correlates with degradation under compression.
does_not_prove: Low-rank compressibility only (not eviction or quantization); per-language degradation numbers not in abstract.
bearing: multilingual/domain dependence of compressibility; predictor of degradation

title: The Sparse Frontier: Sparse Attention Trade-offs in Transformer LLMs
venue: arXiv 2504.17768 (ACL 2026 Findings per ACL Anthology preview)
quote: longer sequences tolerate higher sparsity, suggesting that fixed-budget methods in production are suboptimal
proves: Largest training-free sparse attention study (6 methods, 9 tasks, up to 128K): prefill selection choice is task-dependent; fixed budgets are suboptimal across lengths.
does_not_prove: Accuracy/compute analysis; no serving throughput under mixed workloads.
bearing: task dependence; fixed-budget critique

title: Twilight: Adaptive Attention Sparsity with Hierarchical Top-p Pruning
quote: fails to account for the dynamic nature of real-world scenarios, where the optimal balance between accuracy and efficiency can vary greatly
proves: Top-p (mass-based) budget makes any sparse attention adaptive per input; prunes up to 98% tokens, 3.9x per-token latency.
does_not_prove: Adaptive budget means cost becomes input-dependent; abstract does not evaluate worst-case (dense-attention) inputs or batch-level variance.
bearing: adaptive budget; input-dependent cost (resource-variance risk)

title: FlexPrefill: A Context-Aware Sparse Attention Mechanism for Efficient Long-Sequence Inference
quote: dynamically adjusts sparse attention patterns and computational budget in real-time to meet the specific requirements of each input and attention head
proves: Input-adaptive prefill sparsity using JS divergence and cumulative-attention thresholds.
does_not_prove: Prefill compute only; compute becomes input-dependent; no serving or adversarial worst-case analysis.
bearing: adaptive budget; input-dependent cost

title: Adaptive KV-Cache Compression without Manually Setting Budget (GVote)
venue: arXiv 2509.03136 (ICLR 2026 per search summary, not confirmed)
quote: they force diverse workloads into fixed compression ratios, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and inference performance
proves: Sampled future queries set the per-input cache budget; 2x memory reduction on GSM8K, RULER, LongBench.
does_not_prove: Memory per request becomes input-dependent; no serving-level capacity planning or worst-case input study.
bearing: adaptive budget; fixed-ratio critique

title: ReFreeKV: Towards Threshold-Free KV Cache Compression
quote: the dependence of such input-sensitive threshold can be a fundamental limitation that causes large degradation on arbitrary inputs
proves: States that fixed budgets tuned per domain degrade on arbitrary open-domain inputs; proposes adaptive threshold-free budget across 13 datasets.
does_not_prove: Accuracy-centric; memory variance per request in serving not analyzed.
bearing: direct robustness framing: input-sensitive budgets; adaptive budget

title: DynamicKV: Task-Aware Adaptive KV Cache Compression for Long Context LLMs
quote: we observe distinct activation patterns across layers in various tasks
proves: Layer activation patterns differ by task; task-adaptive per-layer budgets; 1.7% KV keeps ~85% LongBench.
does_not_prove: No serving evaluation.
bearing: task-dependent layer budgets

title: LAVa: Layer-wise KV Cache Eviction with Dynamic Budget Allocation
quote: dynamic layer budgets are crucial for generation tasks (e.g., code completion), while dynamic head budgets play a key role in extraction tasks (e.g., extractive QA)
proves: Which budget dimension matters depends on task type (generation vs extraction); other methods' rankings shift across task types.
does_not_prove: No serving evaluation.
bearing: per-task variance of eviction policy rankings

title: CAKE: Cascading and Adaptive KV Cache Eviction with Layer Preferences
quote: CAKE assesses layer-specific preferences by considering attention dynamics in both spatial and temporal dimensions
proves: Input-adaptive layer budgets; 3.2% KV on LongBench/NeedleBench; >10x decode latency speedup at 128K.
does_not_prove: No serving-level batching study.
bearing: adaptive per-layer budgets

title: Not All Heads Matter: A Head-Level KV Cache Compression Method with Integrated Retrieval and Reasoning (HeadKV)
quote: estimating their importance for contextual QA tasks that require both retrieval and reasoning capabilities
proves: Head budgets estimated offline for contextual QA; 1.5% KV gives 97% of full on contextual QA.
does_not_prove: Head importance tuned for QA; RLKV later shows such retrieval-tuned head selection fails on reasoning.
bearing: offline head budgets; task-specific calibration

title: CompilerKV: Risk-Adaptive KV Compression via Offline Experience Compilation
quote: these signals exhibit far higher cross-prompt regularity than within-prompt signal-to-noise
proves: Online per-prompt sensitivity estimates are noisy; offline-compiled tables transfer across disjoint corpora (Spearman 0.90); under 512/32k budget, SnapKV ~38 vs CompilerKV ~73 vs FullKV ~79 on 128k RULER; batch-16 feasible where FullKV OOMs.
does_not_prove: Transfer tested across corpora, not across task types like reasoning or multilingual; no adversarial inputs.
bearing: calibration transfer evidence; budget-pressure amplification

title: KV-COBRA: KV Cache Compression via Co-Optimized Bit-Rank Allocation
quote: each head has a different optimal mix of rank truncation and quantization
proves: Per-head bit/rank allocation; paper (per search snippet) reports calibration on Python vs WikiText-2 moves HumanEval by at most 1.6 points.
does_not_prove: Calibration-transfer claim seen only in search snippet; abstract does not state it.
bearing: calibration robustness (counter-evidence: allocation transfers)

title: CodeComp: Structural KV Cache Compression for Agentic Coding
quote: systematically discarding structurally critical tokens such as call sites, branch conditions, and assignments
proves: Attention-only eviction drops code-structural tokens; program-analysis priors fix it; integrates into SGLang agentic coding pipelines.
does_not_prove: Code-specific; no throughput-under-load data in abstract.
bearing: code workload failure mode; SGLang integration

title: KVDiagnosis: A Diagnostic Benchmark for KV-Cache Compression in Long-Context Language Models
quote: aggregate task scores reveal neither which correct executions fail nor why
proves: Per-instance failure diagnosis: 12,520 full-correct/compressed-wrong rows on Qwen3-8B; diagnostics separate failures (AUROC 0.684-0.871).
does_not_prove: Accuracy diagnostics only; one model.
bearing: per-instance failure prediction (could seed a robustness monitor)

title: SCOPE: Optimizing Key-Value Cache Compression in Long-context Generation
quote: Deviation of heavy hitters occurs in the reasoning tasks with long outputs
proves: Prefill-only compression and fixed heavy hitters break on long-output tasks (LongGenBench); separate prefill/decode policies.
does_not_prove: No serving evaluation.
bearing: long-output workload shift

title: RetroInfer: A Vector Storage Engine for Scalable Long-Context LLM Inference
quote: prior sparse attention approaches struggle to balance accuracy and retrieval cost due to varying sparsity patterns
proves: Varying sparsity patterns across inputs hurt prior sparse attention; accuracy-bounded vector index gives up to 4.4x decode throughput at 120K.
does_not_prove: Long-context single-request focus; no mixed workload serving.
bearing: sparsity varies by input; offload system
